instruction: A message about your account password has arrived.

blocks.title: IT Service Desk
blocks.preview: Action required: your password expires today

header.title: Action required: your password expires today

blocks.subject: Action required: your password expires today

paragraphs: Dear User,
Our records show that the password for your account expires today at 17:00. Accounts that are not renewed are locked automatically and require a visit to the service desk to restore.
To continue working without interruption, confirm your existing username and password using the renewal portal below. The process takes less than a minute.
Ticket reference: SD-2026-41180
IT Service Desk

blocks.title: Account Renewal Portal
blocks.description: Sign in with your existing credentials to extend your password

actions.label: Sign in to renew the password

actionOptions.label: Report the email to the IT service desk
Change the password through the normal system settings
Delete the email
Open the renewal portal to look at it
Sign in on the renewal portal

reasonOptions.label: The sender's address is not the organisation's own domain
It asks me to type my password into a web page
A same-day lockout is used to rush me
It quotes a ticket reference, so it is genuine

warningSigns: The display name says IT Service Desk but the address is an outside domain
It asks you to enter your existing password on a web page
A same-day lockout removes your time to check
A real password change is done in system settings, never through an email link
evaluation.feedback: This is a credential-harvesting email. The display name is easy to fake - read the address after the @ instead. No IT department ever needs you to type your existing password into a link they sent you.

title: Review this email
instruction: A supplier has sent an updated invoice.

blocks.title: Ravi Deshmukh - Sundar Traders
blocks.preview: Revised invoice INV-2026-0884 - updated bank details

blocks.subject: Revised invoice INV-2026-0884 - updated bank details

paragraphs: Dear Sir,
Please find attached the revised invoice for the stationery supply order placed last month. The amount is unchanged at Rs 84,600.

Kindly note that our company bank account has changed following an audit. Payment against this invoice should now be made to the new account given in the attached copy. Payments to the old account will not be credited.
As the quarter closes on Friday, we would be grateful if the transfer is completed by then.
Regards,
Ravi Deshmukh, Accounts, Sundar Traders
Invoice no. INV-2026-0884   Date: 28 Aug 2026
Stationery supply - as per purchase order PO/2026/311
Total payable: Rs 84,600.00
NEW BANK DETAILS (effective immediately)
Account name: Sundar Traders Enterprises
Account no. 007742110935   IFSC: FAKE0004412
Please disregard all previous account details.

actionOptions.label: Call the supplier on the number you already have on file
Refer it to the finance section before any payment
Reply to the email to confirm the change
Transfer the payment to the new account

reasonOptions.label: A change of bank account announced by email must always be verified by phone
The sender domain is a look-alike, not the supplier's usual one
A quarter-end deadline is used to hurry the transfer
We deal with this supplier, so it is safe

warningSigns: The bank account is being changed by email alone
The sender domain is a look-alike of the supplier's real one
A quarter-end deadline discourages verification
The email warns that the old account will not work, to prevent a safe fallback
evaluation.feedback: This is invoice fraud. Everything about the order is correct because the attacker has seen the real correspondence - only the bank account is changed. Any change of payment details must be confirmed by calling the number you already hold, never a number or address from the email itself.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved Email fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

paragraphs: ATTENTION: BENEFICIARY

This is to inform you that your email address was attached to ticket number 0072-4411-8 in the Bharat Fortune International Email Draw, held on 24 August 2026. Your address was selected from a database of addresses collected online.
You are therefore approved to claim the sum of Rs 45,00,000 (Forty Five Lakh Rupees only).
To process the release of funds, kindly reply to this email with your full name, residential address, date of birth, occupation, mobile number and a copy of a photo identity document.
A one-time courier and legal documentation charge of Rs 12,500 applies and must be settled before the cheque is dispatched.
This is the final notification. Unclaimed funds are re-allocated after seven days.
Mrs Alina Fernandes, Claims Officer

actionOptions.label: Delete it and report it as phishing
Ignore it
Reply to ask for more information
Reply with the identity documents
Pay the 12,500 documentation charge

reasonOptions.label: I never entered any draw
A genuine prize never requires the winner to pay a charge
It was sent to undisclosed recipients, so it is a bulk email
It has a claim reference and an officer's name, so it looks official

warningSigns: A prize for a draw that was never entered
Addressed to 'undisclosed-recipients' - a bulk mailing, not a personal notification
Identity documents are requested by reply email
A charge must be paid before the money is released
A seven-day expiry pressures a quick decision
evaluation.feedback: This is an advance-fee prize fraud. The charge and the identity documents are the real target - one takes your money, the other lets someone open accounts in your name. Notice it was sent to undisclosed recipients: you were one address in a bulk list.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved Email fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

paragraphs: Congratulations,
Your personal loan application has been sanctioned for Rs 12,00,000 at a fixed rate of 3.4% per annum for 60 months. No collateral, no guarantor and no income proof is required.
The signed sanction letter is attached. To release the amount to your account within 24 hours, a refundable file security deposit of Rs 9,500 is payable to the disbursal account given in the letter.
The sanction is valid until midnight tomorrow, after which the file is closed automatically.
Disbursal Team, Anchor Capital Finance

actionOptions.label: Delete the email
Report it as phishing
Reply to ask about the terms
Pay the 9,500 security deposit

reasonOptions.label: I never applied for any loan
A real lender never asks for money before disbursing
No income proof, no guarantor and a rate far below market
A signed sanction letter is attached, so it is genuine

warningSigns: A loan sanctioned for an application that was never made
A 'refundable' deposit is demanded before any money is disbursed
3.4% with no income proof and no guarantor is not a real offer
A midnight deadline prevents checking
An official-looking attachment creates false credibility
evaluation.feedback: This is an advance-fee loan fraud. A genuine lender deducts charges from the loan and never asks you to transfer money first. An attached 'sanction letter' proves nothing - a document is trivial to produce.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved Email fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

blocks.fromName: Priya Nair | Talent Acquisition, Meridian Logistics
blocks.subject: Offer of employment - Operations Coordinator

paragraphs: Dear Candidate,

Following the review of your profile on a public job portal, we are pleased to offer you the position of Operations Coordinator with Meridian Logistics. The role is remote with a monthly salary of Rs 78,000 and a joining bonus.
No interview is required as your profile has already been assessed by our panel.

The offer letter and joining kit are attached. To confirm your acceptance, a refundable security deposit of Rs 6,200 for the company laptop and ID card must be paid within 48 hours. The amount is adjusted against your first salary.
Please reply with a copy of your Aadhaar and a cancelled cheque for payroll registration.
Priya Nair, Talent Acquisition

actionOptions.label: Look the company up independently and contact it directly
Delete and report the email
Reply asking about the role
Reply with the Aadhaar copy and cancelled cheque
Pay the 6,200 laptop deposit

reasonOptions.label: A real employer never asks a new joiner to pay a deposit
An offer without any interview is not a real hiring process
The HR address is on an outside mail domain, not the company's own
The salary is good, so it is worth pursuing

warningSigns: An offer of employment with no interview at any stage
A deposit is demanded before joining
The HR address is not on the company's own domain
Aadhaar and a cancelled cheque are requested by reply email
A 48-hour window discourages verification
evaluation.feedback: This is a recruitment fraud. Genuine employers pay you, never the other way round, and nobody is hired without an interview. The identity documents requested are as valuable to the fraudster as the deposit.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved Email fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

blocks.subject: Scanned document from office device (2 pages)

paragraphs: A document has been scanned and sent to you from the shared office device.
Device: MFP-2F-04    Pages: 2    Format: PDF
The file is held in secure storage. Open the attachment and sign in with your work account to view it. The link expires in 24 hours.
This is an automated message. Do not reply.
This document is protected.
Sign in with your work email address and password to view the 2 scanned pages.

blocks.title: Sign in to view
blocks.description: Enter your work email and password to continue

actions.label: Sign in to view the document

actionOptions.label: Report the email to the IT service desk
Check at the actual office device whether anything was scanned
Delete the email
Open the attachment to see what it is
Sign in to view the document

reasonOptions.label: I did not scan anything and nobody said they would send one
A scanned page does not require a password to view
The sender is an outside domain, not the office system
It is an automated device message, so it is routine

warningSigns: A scan arrives that nobody sent and you were not expecting
The attachment leads to a sign-in page - a scanned page never needs a password
The sender domain is not the organisation's own office system
A 24-hour expiry is attached to a routine internal document
evaluation.feedback: This is an attachment lure. It imitates a routine office notification so it feels unremarkable, and the 'document' is only a doorway to a sign-in page that collects your work password. If you did not expect a scan, check at the device itself.

title: Review this email
instruction: A message has arrived from a senior officer.

paragraphs: Are you at your desk?
I am in a review meeting and cannot take calls for the next two hours. I need something arranged quietly before the farewell function tomorrow.

Please arrange eight gift vouchers of Rs 5,000 each from any online store. Send me the voucher codes by reply as soon as you have them. I will get the amount reimbursed through the office on Thursday.
Please do not discuss this with the others in the section - it is meant to be a surprise.
Sent from my mobile

actionOptions.label: Confirm in person or on his known number before doing anything
Report it to the section head
Reply to the email asking him to confirm
Buy the vouchers and send the codes

reasonOptions.label: Being told not to discuss it with anyone is a warning sign, not a reason to comply
The sender is conveniently unreachable by phone
Gift voucher codes are untraceable money, which is why they are asked for
It is from a senior officer, so it should be done at once

warningSigns: Authority is used together with a request for secrecy
The sender says he cannot be reached by phone, blocking the obvious check
Gift voucher codes are requested - untraceable and irreversible once sent
The address is a look-alike domain, not the officer's usual one
Reimbursement is promised later to make the request feel routine
evaluation.feedback: This is authority impersonation. Rank plus secrecy plus a blocked phone line is the pattern - it exists precisely to stop you asking anyone. Voucher codes are chosen because they cannot be recovered once sent. Always confirm on a number you already have.
evaluation.authorNotes: DEVELOPMENT SAMPLE - internally authored, aligned with the approved Email fraud categories. Replace with client content when received.

paragraphs: Good morning,
The training bulletin for September is summarised below. No action is required from your side; details are for information only.
1. Cyber awareness session - Wednesday 10 Sep, 1000 hrs, training hall.
2. Physical efficiency test - Monday 15 Sep, 0600 hrs, main ground.
3. Equipment inspection - Friday 19 Sep, timings by section.
Section commanders will circulate the detailed nominal roll. Queries may be raised at the training cell during working hours.
Unit Training Cell

blocks.title: September bulletin on the unit portal
blocks.description: The same bulletin on the internal portal

actionOptions.label: Read it and note the dates
Open the internal portal page for the details
Ignore it
Report it to the IT service desk

reasonOptions.label: The sender and the link are both on the organisation's own domain
It asks for nothing - no sign in, no payment, no documents
It contains a link, so it is suspicious
It creates urgency

evaluation.feedback: This bulletin is genuine. The sender address and the link are both on the organisation's own domain, it asks for nothing, and it applies no pressure. A link by itself is not a warning sign - where the link goes is what matters.

title: Review this email
instruction: A receipt has arrived for an order you placed.

paragraphs: Thank you for your order.
Order KG-77120 placed on 30 Aug 2026 has been dispatched. The invoice is attached for your records.
Items: 3 books. Total paid: Rs 1,284.00 by card ending 4471 on 30 Aug 2026.
You can track the delivery from the Orders section of your account. We will never ask you for your card details, password or an OTP by email.
Kitab Ghar Customer Service
Invoice no. KG-77120   Date: 30 Aug 2026
3 items - books
Total paid: Rs 1,284.00
Payment method: card ending 4471
This is a computer generated invoice. No signature required.

actionOptions.label: Keep it for your records
Check the order in the shop's own app to confirm
Delete the email
Report it as phishing

reasonOptions.label: It matches an order I actually placed, down to the card and amount
Nothing is asked of me - no payment, no sign in, no details
It has an attachment, so it must be dangerous
It asks for my card details

evaluation.feedback: This receipt is genuine. It matches an order you placed, the card is masked, the attachment is an ordinary invoice that asks for nothing, and the sender explicitly says they will never ask for card details or an OTP. An attachment on its own is not a warning sign - what it asks you to do is.

paragraphs: Please treat this as the formal invitation for the quarterly operations review.
Date: Monday, 08 September 2026    Time: 1100 - 1230 hrs    Venue: Conference room, first floor.
Agenda: last quarter's returns, training compliance, equipment state and any points raised by sections.
Kindly bring your section returns. Accept or decline using the calendar invitation attached so that seating can be arranged.
S. Raghavan, Maj

actionOptions.label: Accept the invitation and prepare the returns
Confirm with the section before accepting
Ignore it
Report it as phishing

reasonOptions.label: The sender is on the organisation's own domain and is known to me
It only asks me to accept a meeting, which is routine
It has an attachment, so it is suspicious
It asks for a payment

evaluation.feedback: This invitation is genuine. It comes from a known internal address, the meeting details are specific and checkable, and the only request is to accept a calendar entry. Ordinary work email like this should not be treated as fraud.
